name: Recombination to Centimorgans
seoDesc: Recombination frequency undercounts true genetic distance, because a double crossover between two loci reverts the markers to parental type. Free recombinatio
summary:
Recombination frequency undercounts true genetic distance, because a double crossover between two loci reverts the markers to parental type. It returns recombination fraction, haldane distance, kosambi distance and corrected distance (chosen function), and the panel shows all of them at once.

A mapping function corrects for it: Haldane's assumes no interference, Kosambi's assumes some. Both turn a recombination fraction into centimorgans. Press Calculate and the results appear in the grey boxes; after the first press they keep up with every edit, so there is no page to reload. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Recombination to Centimorgans
sections.html:
RF = recombinants ÷ total. Haldane: d = −½ ln(1 − 2·RF). Kosambi: d = ¼ ln[(1 + 2RF) ÷ (1 − 2RF)]. Both in Morgans, ×100 for cM

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
RFrecombination fraction, between 0 and 0.5—
cMcentimorgan: 1 cM is 1% recombination—
interferencethe tendency of one crossover to suppress the next nearby—

sections.title: How do I use the Recombination to Centimorgans?
sections.html:
Every input sits in the same order the formula is written, so the page reads like the equation.

  1. Enter the recombinant and total offspring from the cross.
  2. Tick Kosambi if your organism shows interference — the usual choice outside fungi.
  3. Read the recombination fraction and the corrected distance in centimorgans.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: recombinant offspring of 35, total offspring of 200, use kosambi (interference) of 0.

Substituting them into the formula gives recombination fraction of 0.175, haldane distance of 21.54 cM, kosambi distance of 18.27 cM, corrected distance (chosen function) of 21.54 cM, distance added by the map correction of 4.04 cM.

Those numbers come from the same solver the page runs in your browser, not from an illustration, so typing different inputs moves the answer exactly as the arithmetic says.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
The number on its own is not a judgement. These are the bands most often used when the result is quoted in a paper, a report or a label:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
under 10 cMTightly linkedfew double crossovers; either function works
10 – 30 cMLinkedthe two functions begin to differ
50 cM or moreEffectively unlinkedat RF 0.5 the distance is undefined

  • Recombination fraction saturates at 0.5: two loci on different chromosomes recombine 50% of the time, and the same is true of two loci far apart on the same chromosome.

  • Haldane's function assumes crossovers are independent; Kosambi's assumes interference, which is closer to what is seen in most eukaryotes.

  • Map distance is not physical distance: recombination hotspots make one megabase worth anywhere from 0.1 to 10 cM.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
These are the errors that account for almost every wrong answer people bring to this calculator:

  • Reporting the recombination fraction as centimorgans for distant loci, which understates the distance badly.
  • Using Haldane on data where interference is strong.
  • Forgetting that 50% recombination means unlinked, not 50 cM apart.

faq.q: What is the difference between Haldane and Kosambi?
faq.a: Haldane assumes crossovers are independent; Kosambi assumes they interfere, so it converts the same RF to a shorter distance.
Because beyond about 50 cM the recombination fraction stops rising — the loci behave as if unlinked.
A 1% chance of recombination between two loci in a generation.

faq.q: What does the Recombination to Centimorgans actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns recombination fraction, haldane distance, kosambi distance and corrected distance (chosen function). Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
